answers.rationale: A best matches Erin's repeated preference for an afternoon-friendly itinerary with one reasonably short connection and schedule simplicity over a small fare difference. B saves only $18 but imposes a 3-hour-15-minute layover and much later arrival; C adds a second connection; D requires a much earlier departure and has the tightest layover.

A clears Erin's usual 4.0-plus review threshold, has the needed pool and fitness room, free parking, and a short site drive. She repeatedly accepts a missing hot tub when the closer, better-reviewed work hotel otherwise covers the core amenities. B and D fall below her usual rating floor, while C gives up pool access and adds commute/parking friction.

A is the closest strong-review option that provides both pool and fitness access with uncomplicated parking. Erin has consistently favored this combination over a marginally shorter but sub-4.0 hotel with a hot tub, or a higher-rated but farther property that sacrifices pool access and adds parking cost.

A best fits Erin and Mark's recurring leisure-trip priority set: a solid review score, easy parking, and the complete recovery package of pool, hot tub, and fitness, while remaining close enough to the organized ride. Erin treats balconies and walkable dinner as valuable bonuses, but not as reasons to sacrifice the core recovery amenities or accept sub-4.0 ratings. B and D miss her usual review floor; C is appealing for rating, balcony, and dinner access but lacks both pool and hot tub.
